subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Should the permanent fix preserve paragraph boundaries by consolidating one in-band separator PR now, or require explicit boundary metadata before merging a fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the chosen boundary contract affects shared block-streaming delivery semantics and two open closing PRs already propose overlapping text-based repairs.

options.title: Consolidate one separator-preserving PR
options.body: Review one linked PR as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction and coalescer no-double-separator coverage including maxChars boundaries, and close the other PR as superseded after choosing the viable path.

options.title: Require boundary metadata first
options.body: Pause the text-based PRs until paragraph/newline/hard-split metadata is designed and tested through chunking, coalescing, and delivery.

options.title: Reject the current direction
options.body: Close or redirect the linked PRs and keep this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored redesign of streaming boundary semantics.

recommendation.title: Consolidate one separator-preserving PR
recommendation.body: Review one linked PR as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction and coalescer no-double-separator coverage including maxChars boundaries, and close the other PR as superseded after choosing the viable path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and refined the paragraph streaming behavior that defines the boundary contract under review.
